alignments.note: The optative formula מִי יִתֵּן takes its fixed English rendering *Oh that* (rules 17, 30); no morpheme's own lexeme is written in it, so the source head is the deterministic first token (rule 6). The ASV rewrites the *that* over the coordinated clause, so that occurrence joins the same discontinuous unit (rules 55, 25).
Suffix takes the subject pronoun of the possessive recasting, rewritten over the coordinated clause (rules 43, 25).
The possessive preposition is what makes the clause possessive and carries the *had*, rewritten over the coordinated clause (rules 43, 25).
Anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied noun phrase and infinitive marker, headed on the lexeme (rules 46, 52).
The ASV writes a bare object for the participle, leaving the preposition's relation unstated (rule 40).
Presentative particle rendered *Lo here*, headed on the lexical anchor.
Predicate noun with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20); the margin's literal *mark* is set aside (rule 38).
Jussive frame with the lexical verb, discontinuous around the subject (rule 25).
Noun with the supplied *the* (rule 15); the margin's literal *book* is set aside.
Relative supplied for a finite clause juxtaposed to a written antecedent; no relative morpheme stands in the Hebrew (rules 46, 55).
Generic head noun plus its construct dependent rendered by one English word, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme (rule 30).

review_notes: The italicized *that I had* in the second half is read as the one optative formula and the possessive recasting rewritten over the coordinated clause (rules 55, 25, 43); the competing reading marks all three words `added`.
Both marginal glosses ("Hebrew mark", "Hebrew book") were read and set aside (rule 38).
